items.q: The drug list of 2° FSGS includes pamidronate, anabolic steroids, heroin, sirolimus, IFN α and the tyrosine kinase inhibitor:
items.exp: Dasatinib (tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI)) among 2° FSGS drugs. (Book p763)

items.q: All of the following sit in the 2° FSGS drug list EXCEPT:
items.exp: Gold belongs to the MN/MCD drug lists; FSGS drugs are pamidronate, anabolic steroids, heroin, sirolimus, dasatinib, IFN α. (Book p763)

items.q: The infection causes of 2° FSGS are HIV-associated nephropathy (HIVAN), parvo B19, EBV and:
items.exp: Infections: HIVAN, parvo B19, EBV, CMV. (Book p763)

items.q: The miscellaneous 2° FSGS causes are sickle cell anemia, obesity and:
items.exp: Miscellaneous: sickle cell anemia, obesity, congenital cyanotic heart disease. (Book p763)

items.q: 1° FSGS is antigen-associated: soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR) and cardiotrophin-like cytokine 1 (CLC-1) together act as:
items.exp: suPAR + CLC-1 bracketed as circulating permeability factor. (Book p763)

items.q: Match each genetic form with its gene product — 1) NPHS1 gene 2) NPHS2 gene 3) α actin 4, TRPC 6 … A) Podocin B) Nephrin C) Autosomal dominant adolescent form
items.exp: NPHS1 → nephrin; NPHS2 → podocin; α actin 4, TRPC 6 = autosomal dominant. (Book p763)

items.q: Match each congenital-NS column with its feature — 1) NPHS1 histology 2) NPHS2 histology 3) α actin 4 / TRPC 6 inheritance … A) Autosomal dominant B) Diffuse mesangial sclerosis C) FSGS
items.exp: NPHS1: present at birth, diffuse mesangial sclerosis; NPHS2: by 3-5 years, FSGS; α actin 4/TRPC 6: autosomal dominant, adolescents. (Book p763)

items.q: The genetic forms of congenital nephrotic syndrome are resistant to immunosuppression therapy; the only Rx written is:
items.exp: Resistant to immunosuppression therapy; only Rx: transplantation. (Book p763)

items.q: 2° perihilar FSGS follows removal of a pathological kidney because the remaining nephrons/other kidney undergo:
items.exp: Removal of pathological kidney → remaining nephrons undergo hyperfiltration injury (glomerular hypertrophy) → 2° perihilar FSGS. (Book p763)

items.q: 2° perihilar FSGS runs a slow course with good prognosis and asymptomatic proteinuria; its causes are VUR, U/l RAS and stone/mass, and progression can be slowed using:
items.exp: Causes: VUR, U/l RAS, stone/mass; progression can be slowed using ACE (−). (Book p763)
